sections.h2: Who to call about a Madison County tax bill
sections.html:
Three Richmond offices split the work. The sheriff answers for the bill, the PVA answers for the value behind it, and the County Clerk answers for deeds and for overdue bills.

  • Sheriff: 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, Richmond, reached at 859-623-1511. Bills can be searched and paid through a secure portal, at the counter, or by post, and cash should never go in an envelope.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption paperwork, at 859-623-5410.
  • Clerk: deeds are filed at the Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave. The Berea branch at 304 Chestnut Street serves vehicle and marriage license customers.

An heir or agent can settle a bill ahead of a sale too, because KRS 134.119 lets the sheriff accept money from a third party for the owner.

sections.h2: Housing and land in Madison County
sections.html:
Madison County is a college county that has been adding residents for decades. Eastern Kentucky University is in Richmond and Berea College is in Berea, the county's only two cities. Population was 82,916 in 2010 and 92,701 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 101,696, a gain of 9.7 percent over April 2020.

The county has 42,389 housing units. Owners live in 62.0 percent of homes, the typical owner-occupied home is worth $232,000, and typical gross rent is $889. Roughly 36 percent of residents were rural at the 2020 census, so plenty of sellers own land around Kingston, Waco or Speedwell rather than inside a city.

Appraisal of a farm follows what its soil earns, and a subdivision developer's offer plays no part. That is the rule in Section 172A of the state constitution. Ask the PVA to show how each of your acres is classified before you price a farm.

Trust the periods shown on your own bill or in the portal. The ordinary timetable sits in KRS 134.015.

Typical Kentucky payment stages
Payment periodWhat you owe
By November 1Face amount minus two percent
Following two months, through DecemberFace amount
JanuaryFace amount plus five percent
February onwardFace amount plus ten percent of the unpaid tax

A late-printed bill gets a compressed schedule from the Department of Revenue, counted from the mailing date. Fees pile onto delinquent bills, and one percent interest per month starts after the transfer to the clerk.

The Clerk's website carries the delinquent county property tax list and a third-party purchaser page. Search for your parcel before you list. The County Attorney's office also runs delinquent collection, and an installment agreement signed before the Clerk's sale keeps a bill from being bought by an investor. Its number is 624-4777, extension 9.

A sit-down with the PVA comes first. When it settles nothing, you file a petition at the Clerk's office and the county board takes the case, as laid out in KRS 133.120. Carry sales data, an appraisal or insurance records, and keep paying on your own number during the dispute.

Close to either campus, nearby recent sales of similar houses make the strongest comparables. On acreage, ask which agricultural class the PVA applied. KRS 133.030 has the board meet between 25 and 35 days following inspection.

Madison County offers one. The deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100 off the assessed value. It is open to owner-occupants who are 65 or older or classified as totally disabled, and the Madison County PVA takes the application. A buyer who qualifies files separately after closing.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you list
sections.html:
A short checklist keeps a tax question from surfacing at the closing table. Work through it in order and you will know your exact position before a buyer does.

  • Search your parcel on the sheriff's portal and note whether the current bill is paid.
  • Check the Clerk's delinquent list for earlier years, and call the Clerk's office if your parcel appears.
  • Ask the PVA how your property is classified and whether an exemption is on file in your name.
  • Request a written payoff from each office that holds a balance, and ask how long each figure stays good.
  • Give those letters to the title agent so the amounts come out of your proceeds at the closing.

If you inherited the house, confirm whose name the tax roll shows. If the roll still carries the prior owner, the bill goes to that name, so ask the PVA about a name and address change before you list. A buyer's title examiner will find an open lien no matter who is named on the roll, so settle it early rather than at the last minute.

Cash buyers often move faster than the offices do. Tax payoffs, a recorded deed and a notarized price certificate each take their own turn at a counter, so start gathering them as soon as you accept an offer.

Get a payoff figure from the sheriff for this year's bill and scan the clerk's delinquent list for earlier years. Property taxes are commonly prorated between buyer and seller, with the current owner answerable for payment, so check how your settlement statement divides the bill.

A tax lien can ride with the land for as long as eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), which is why title agents ask for payoff at the table.

Deeds go to the Clerk's Richmond Branch at (859) 624-4703, extension 3. The office keeps papers from 1786 onward, searchable by a person's name only, and has scanned everything since 1986 for viewing in person or through the paid ECCLIX service. Electronic filings are handled each morning until roughly 10:00. Owners can also enroll in DocAlert, a free notification that fires whenever a document is recorded under their name or property details.

The state's transfer tax is fifty cents for each $500 of value under KRS 142.050, paid when the deed is filed. Ask the closing agent to show it on the settlement statement. If you plan a cash sale, line up the payoff letters and the signed deed early so the closing is not delayed by a tax or recording question.

faqs.q: Can Madison County property tax be paid online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the sheriff's secure portal, which also lets you search bills. The portal displays any processing fee before you confirm, and paying at the Richmond office or by mail still works.

faqs.q: How large is the 2026 exemption for Madison County seniors?
faqs.a: It is $49,100, the same as for 2025. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply through the PVA.

faqs.q: Which Madison County office records a deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk's Richmond Branch at 321 N. Madison Ave. Call (859) 624-4703, extension 3, for the recordings desk.

faqs.q: Is there help when a Madison County bill has gone delinquent?
faqs.a: The County Attorney's delinquent tax program, at 624-4777 extension 9, can arrange installment payments if you sign before the Clerk's sale.

faqs.q: Who pays the Madison County tax bill when a house changes owners mid-year?
faqs.a: The current owner must make sure it is paid, and bills are commonly prorated at closing. Confirm the split with your closing agent.
